claims.text: A conformal 1–2 nm CeO2 coating will enhance low-temperature oxidation activity relative to the unmodified catalyst.
A conformal 1–2 nm CeO2 coating will reduce poisoning by H2O.
A conformal 1–2 nm CeO2 coating will reduce poisoning by NO.
A conformal 1–2 nm CeO2 coating will improve catalyst durability under simulated automotive exhaust conditions.
Adding the CeO2 coating will retain low platinum-group-metal usage.
ALD deposition will form a continuous, ultrathin CeO2 layer on the catalyst.
The ultrathin CeO2 layer will act as an oxygen buffer.
The ultrathin CeO2 layer will stabilize the catalyst's surface nanostructure.
The CeO2 coating will store and release oxygen at low temperatures.
Low-temperature oxygen storage and release by CeO2 will facilitate oxidation reactions.
Oxygen vacancies in CeO2 will trap H2O and NO poisoning species.
The proposed oxygen-buffering and poison-trapping actions will prevent catalyst sintering.
The proposed oxygen-buffering and poison-trapping actions will prevent catalyst deactivation.
Preventing sintering and deactivation will preserve active sites and enhance durability.
The unmodified near-equiatomic MPE catalyst has lower low-temperature oxidation activity than the proposed coated catalyst.
The unmodified catalyst has greater sensitivity to H2O and NO poisoning than the proposed coated catalyst.
The unmodified catalyst has lower durability under accelerated aging than the proposed coated catalyst.
The predicted benefits will apply during operation below 150 °C, exposure to H2O and NO, and thermal-aging cycles with spikes up to approximately 750 °C.
An excessively thick or non-uniform CeO2 layer may block active sites and eliminate the proposed benefits.
